title: Subordinate Navigation and Manual Fallback Preservation
purpose: Keep the Operator from being trapped by imperfect router state while making the router the primary path.
humanGoal: The Operator should be able to open supporting screens for reference or recovery without mistaking them for the current workflow step. The current-action panel remains the boss. Supporting screens are tools.
summary: Correct subordinate/manual navigation so secondary screens remain reachable as fallback or supporting views, but no longer function as the primary workflow model. Provide clear labels, a return path to the routed action, and non-mutating support navigation while preserving WC04 repair behavior.
includedScope: Make supporting navigation visibly subordinate to the routed current action.
Preserve manual navigation as an Alpha escape hatch.
Provide a clear return path to the routed current action.
Ensure manual support-screen selection does not mutate durable workflow state.
Remove, collapse, or clarify redundant navigation surfaces where safe.
Handle missing or unresolved route targets with plain-language guidance.
outOfScope: WC06 left-to-right workflow map beyond preserving existing process rail behavior.
Provider SDKs, cloud services, authentication, databases, browser automation, LLM APIs, or unrelated integrations.
acceptanceCriteria: The routed current action remains visually primary after a support screen is opened.
Manual supporting navigation is clearly labeled as support/reference/tooling, not the main workflow.
The UI provides a clear return path to the routed current action.
Opening a support screen does not mutate durable workflow state or imply the current action changed.
The active support screen is visibly identified as a support screen when applicable.
The route-specific primary action remains more prominent than manual browsing.
Redundant navigation controls are removed, collapsed, or clearly differentiated where safe.
Missing or unresolved support routes produce plain-language guidance rather than silent failure.
Existing screens remain reachable unless intentionally replaced by an equivalent path.
Current-action routing does not advance to WC06 or later work prematurely.
No WC06-WC15 behavior is implemented prematurely.
Automated validation passes or skipped checks are documented.
validationExpectations: Read AGENTS.md and docs/dev/VALIDATION_COMMAND_LANES.md before validation.
Run the normal Windows validation lane.
Run existing current-action fixture validation if affected.
Run existing WC04 repair fixture validation if affected.
Run focused navigation/support-screen fixture validation if feasible.
Run local safety scan before staging.
handoffPromptSummary: Implement only WC05 from clean dev on feature/phase-03-wc05-subordinate-navigation-fallback. Make supporting/manual navigation subordinate to the current-action router, preserve escape hatch access, provide a return path to the routed action, clarify support-screen state, preserve WC04 repairs, and do not implement WC06-WC15.
